### Jonathan’s Covenant with David
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier.org
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/jonathans-covenant-with-david
Passage: 1 Samuel 20:16
Points:
- Unlike his erratic father Saul, Jonathan demonstrated wisdom, humility, and selfless loyalty toward David.
- Acknowledging God's hand on David, Jonathan forged a covenant to secure lasting safety for his own descendants.
- David pledged enduring covenant love (*hesed*) rather than seeking the customary elimination of a rival king's lineage.
- Jonathan risked his own royal inheritance and physical safety to discover Saul's plans and warn his friend.
- Believers are urged to mirror this covenant loyalty by actively pursuing one another's welfare in the church.

### Living in Light of Your Testimony
Author: Michael Youssef, Ph.D.
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/leading-the-way/leading-the-way-week-of-august-19-2024.html
Passage: 1 Samuel 20:14-15
Points:
- Overwhelmed by Saul's hostility, David momentarily forgot God's past deliverance and succumbed to anxiety.
- David relied on human cunning rather than divine guidance, devising a deceptive excuse for missing the New Moon meal.
- The biblical narrative transparently details David's missteps to remind readers that even men after God's heart can stumble.
- Jonathan stood by David in covenant faithfulness, agreeing to test Saul's temper and signal the outcome in the field.
- Believers navigating circumstances beyond their control should reject self-pity and remember the Lord's proven faithfulness.

### Day 25: 1 Samuel 20:1–17
Author: Beth Moore
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/plus/books/portraits-of-devotion/portraits-of-devotion-day-25-1-samuel-20-117.html
Passage: 1 Samuel 20:14-15
Points:
- God knits people together through His Spirit to fulfill His sovereign plans during trials.
- Uncommon companions can honestly express panic and raw frustrations without destroying their relationship.
- Jonathan proved his loyalty by validating David's genuine distress rather than becoming defensive about his family.
- The covenant between David and Jonathan bound their households to show God's faithful love to future generations.
- Friendships anchored in God are capable of enduring separation, stress, and intense sorrow.
